title: Order and degree
back: Degree is defined only when the equation is a polynomial in the derivatives. Order and degree, when defined, are positive integers.

title: General and particular solutions
back: General solution: constants present. Particular solution: constants found from given conditions, so none are left.

title: Variables separable
back: Get all $y$ with $dy$ and all $x$ with $dx$, then integrate both sides. One $+C$ is enough.

title: Is it homogeneous?
legend: F = the right-hand side of dy/dx = F(x, y)
back: A function of degree zero. Write this check in the answer: it carries a mark.

title: Homogeneous: the substitution
back: The equation becomes separable in $v$ and $x$. At the end put $v=\dfrac yx$. If $\dfrac xy$ appears, use $x=vy$ instead.

title: Linear equation: integrating factor
legend: P, Q = functions of x only
back: Coefficient of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ must be 1 before you read $P$. Simplify: $e^{\log x}=x$, $e^{2\log x}=x^2$, $e^{-\log x}=\dfrac1x$.

title: Linear equation: solution
back: P goes up (into the I.F.), Q goes in (to the integral).

title: Linear in x
legend: P, Q = functions of y only
back: Try this when the equation is not linear in $y$, for example $(x+2y^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y$.

title: Integrating factors worth knowing
tex: P=\tfrac1x\to x\qquad P=\cot x\to\sin x\qquad P=\tan x\to\sec x

title: Growth and decay
legend: k = constant, found from a second condition
back: "Rate proportional to the amount present" always leads here. Doubling in time $T$ gives $k=\dfrac{\log2}{T}$.
